dct_description_sm: The International Polar Year Inuit Health Survey for Adults collected data on blood concentrations of environmental contaminants in 2 595 participants. Laird et al. compared the observed blood levels with those in the general Canadian population (Canadian Health Measures Survey), previous Inuit environmental studies, and trigger/intervention guideline values from Health Canada, Centers for Disease Control (CDC), or Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) (1). Guidance values were available only for polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs, specifically Arochlor 1260), cadmium, mercury and lead. For all other environmental contaminants (DDE, DDT, toxaphene, chlordane, and PBDEs), the exposure distributions were not interpretable within the context of established or evidence-formulated guidance values. Therefore, the health implications of the observed blood levels for these environmental contaminants are uncertain.  Moreover, the PCB guideline is out dated and the cadmium guideline used is for occupation health.  Therefore, PCB and cadmium need to be re-assessed as well.  The formulation of guidance values will improve our interpretation of the environmental contaminant exposure data. In addition, interpretation of results in the context of screening values will improve knowledge translation because messages will incorporate clear information about priority for following up.  Screening values have been used for some time in occupational exposure assessments. Biomonitoring-based reference values such as the biological exposure indices (BEIs) developed by the American Conference of Governmental Industrial Hygienists (ACGIH) represent the level of an analyte in biological media which is consistent with exposure at a guideline value (e.g. the threshold limit value). However these values are not applicable to the general population exposure due to the specific exposure occurring in workplace (higher concentration, duration of exposure limited to 8hrs, etc)   Therefore, the project is to develop screening values to interpret the biomonitoring results using a combination of BEs and/or or updated international values.  Associated public health action plans, according to age, sex, and level of exposure will be developed similar to the approach that was used for establishing the blood guidance values for methylmercury in Canada.
